messages.text: like another meanwell power supply because i believe the one i have is dead

Hi Adam, I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed this over to me.

Before I line up a replacement supply, I want to be sure the supply is the dead part and not the miner, because the fix is different for each.

One check: plug the MeanWell into the wall on its own, with the DC cable NOT connected to the BS-2.

1. Does its own small LED light up (usually green)?
2. Any clicking, buzzing or smell from it?

Tell me what it does and we go from there.

so i plugged it in and it does nothing theres no sound no spot for a LED (that i can see) theres no audio queue at all. when checking on the firmware of the miner itself its saying the imput voltage is 12.1 volts i have the power supply set to 115v setting on the side and when looking in the OS under the regulator input current its at 0 the connector is a xt30

That 12.1 V reading is important, so let me pin it down before we call the supply dead.

A MeanWell with a 115/230 switch on the side (LRS style) does have a tiny green LED, but it is on the board near the terminals and easy to miss, and it makes no sound at all when healthy. So "no sound, no visible LED" does not by itself mean it is gone.

One check: with the MeanWell plugged into the wall AND the XT30 plugged into the BS-2, is the miner's web UI live on your network right now, and is that 12.1 V updating live on that screen?

If the UI is up and reading 12.1 V, the supply is delivering power and the fault is on the miner side, not the brick.

i was getting a core voltage error on the BS2 original firmware and originally thought it was a firmware bug so i replaced the firmware with the harlo OS firmware and after about 5 minutes the fan stays maxed out even though i have it set to auto and to run at 55 degrees C and does not update on the firmware
Let me check the current Harlo OS version before I call this.
Searched the web · Harlo OS firmware latest version harlolabs

That tells me a lot, and the good news is that your MeanWell is almost certainly fine. If the miner is reading 12.1 V on its input, the brick is delivering 12 V. A new supply would not change anything here.

What the rest points to:

1. Regulator input current 0 means the board is not drawing any power through the core regulator, so the chip never comes up.
2. The fan pinning at 100% and ignoring your auto curve is the firmware's safety fallback when it cannot get a valid temperature or core voltage reading. Harlo OS does that on purpose.
3. The core voltage error survived a full firmware change, from the BitFortun build to Harlo OS, so it is not a firmware bug.

Two things so I can finish this properly:

1. A screenshot of the Harlo OS dashboard showing the readings and the core voltage error.
2. The exact Harlo OS version shown in the UI (Settings or the footer).

Send those and I will put my findings together for the team.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Verdict recorded; Sarah takes it from here.
